title: Two Neighbors Compare Notes on Staying Patient
script: Sri: [tired] Amir, honestly, this year has tested my patience more than any year I can remember.
Amir: [gently] I understand that more than you might think. My own year hasn't been easy either.
Sri: [curious] What happened to you? You always seem so calm at the mosque, greeting everyone with that same warm smile.
Amir: [thoughtful] I lost my job in January. I still haven't found steady work since then.
Sri: [surprised] I had no idea. You never once complained about it, not even quietly.
Amir: [reflective] What would complaining actually fix? It only makes the waiting feel heavier for me and everyone around me.
Sri: [touched] That's a strong way to think. I wish I could manage my own stress that calmly.
Amir: [warmly] It isn't calm every single day, believe me. Some nights I lie awake, worried and frustrated about money.
Sri: [gently] What do you do on those nights?
Amir: [sincere] I pray, and I remind myself that this hardship is temporary, even when it doesn't feel that way.
Sri: [thoughtful] I've been struggling with my mother's illness this year, and some days I feel close to breaking completely.
Amir: [warmly] I noticed you visiting the hospital often. I never asked, because I didn't want to intrude on something private.
Sri: [honestly] I appreciate that, actually. Some people ask too many questions, and it becomes exhausting to keep answering them.
Amir: [gently] For what it's worth, I've seen how patiently you handle her appointments, even while working full time.
Sri: [reflective] Some days patience feels impossible. I snap at small things that don't even matter.
Amir: [understanding] That's normal too. Righteousness isn't about never struggling, it's about returning to patience again after we fail at it.
Sri: [thoughtful] I like that. I always thought righteous people simply never got tired or frustrated at all.
Amir: [warmly] No one is like that, honestly. We just keep quietly trying, and trust that the effort itself matters to Allah.
Sri: [peacefully] Talking with you today actually helped more than you probably realize, Amir.
Amir: [gently] It helped me too, Sri. Sometimes we forget everyone around us is carrying something heavy too.
